To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) evaluative concerns perfectionists experience more distress than do nonperfectionists and that this relation can be fully accounted for by the mediators of perceived social support, avoidant coping and hassles and that (2) personal standards perfectionists experience more anxiety and depression than do nonperfectinists and that this is partially explained by the mediator of active coping.
the evaluative concerns dimension of perfectionism was related to distress via its relation to hassles, avoid ant coping, and perceived lack of social support.

evaluative concerns perfectionists experience more psychological distress because of the greater hassles and less social support they experience, whereas personal standards perfectionists experience less distress because of the active coping they employ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the social environment, particularly the social support available to the individual, in understanding the relations between perfectionism and psychological distress.
the role of perfectionism as a vulnerability factor in the etiology of distress.
the relationship between perfectionism and the experience of psychological distress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perfectionism literature has been dominated by studies examining negative aspects of perfectionism.
perfectionism is a multidimensional construct with a variety of negative outcomes.
the relationship between perfectionism and psychological distress is not straightforward, but is complex and multifaceted (Flett & Hewitt, 2002).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the perfectionism literature is not a unified field.

we found that perfectionism was a risk factor for psychological problems in university students, but that the relation between perfectionism, hassles, and coping was complex, and that perceived social support was a protective factor against distress.
perfectionism has a negative impact on psychological health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many factors that contribute to perfectionism.
there are a number of factors that can influence the relationship between perfectionism and mental health.
perfectionism is associated with a number of psychological problems and that it can be measured reliably.
